blocks.content: The variation in duration of sunlight at different places is due to differences in latitude, altitude, season and duration of the day.

rows: Determines topography, soil nutrients, and drainage, influencing whether land supports agriculture, grasslands, or forests.
Governs thermal vegetation zones, seasonal leaf shedding, tree growth rates, and spatial density of forests.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Relief factors, including land and soil, determine the physical terrain and nutrient availability for vegetation growth.
Temperature along with atmospheric humidity significantly governs the character, distribution, and thermal limits of vegetation zones.
Photoperiod variations due to latitude, altitude, and season lead to faster tree growth during longer summer days.
Precipitation levels directly dictate forest density, where heavy rainfall areas support lush, dense vegetation.
Distinguish between Relief (Land & Soil) and Climate (Temperature, Photoperiod, Precipitation) as primary controlling factors.
Note that longer photoperiod duration during summer months directly accelerates tree growth.
Remember precipitation thresholds determining vegetation types (e.g., >200 cm rainfall for Tropical Evergreen Forests).
